kbdeutscheseck.name: Deutsches Eck
kbdeutscheseck.slogan: Where the Moselle slips into the Rhine under a bronze emperor.
kbdeutscheseck.line: The Empire will never be destroyed, if you are united and loyal.
kbdeutscheseck.by: Max von Schenkendorf, inscription on the Kaiser Wilhelm monument, Koblenz

kbehrenbreitstein.name: Ehrenbreitstein Fortress
kbehrenbreitstein.slogan: A Prussian giant watching two rivers from its cliff.
kbehrenbreitstein.line: Here Ehrenbreitstein, with her shatter'd wall black with the miner's blast, upon her height yet shows of what she was.
kbehrenbreitstein.by: Lord Byron, Childe Harold's Pilgrimage, Canto III, 1816

kbloreley.name: Loreley
kbloreley.slogan: The slate cliff where a golden-haired siren still sings to sailors.
kbloreley.line: The Loreley is a 132-metre slate rock; Heine's 1824 poem made its siren world famous.

kbburgeltz.name: Burg Eltz
kbburgeltz.slogan: Towers stacked like a fairy tale, hidden in a forest bend.
kbburgeltz.line: The House of Eltz has lived here since the 12th century, and the castle appeared on the 500 Deutsche Mark note from 1965 to 1992.

kbmarksburg.name: Marksburg
kbmarksburg.slogan: The one Rhine castle that no army ever brought down.
kbmarksburg.line: Of about 40 hill castles between Bingen and Koblenz, the Marksburg is one of only two never destroyed.
